title: Felix and the Kitchen
premise: Marine biologist Elodie Zhou joins a workplace anonymous pen-pal program to distract herself from a failed engagement, only to be matched with Felix Arden — the ruthless development consultant whose resort project threatens the sea-turtle sanctuary she has spent six years protecting. Through letters that never reveal names, they fall for the stranger on the page while clashing in person over permits, land deals, and buried family debts. When identities are exposed at a public hearing, Elodie must choose between the sanctuary's survival and the man who deceived her, and Felix must decide whether his ambition or his conscience defines him. In the end, Felix walks away from the deal, funds the sanctuary quietly through his final letter, and earns a second chance at Elodie's door — one turtle season later.
about_author: Z. M. Ishikawa is a former environmental policy analyst who traded briefing papers for love stories set against disappearing coastlines. They write from a small house near the water, where every novel begins with a real conservation battle.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Opening on a night survey of nesting loggerheads, we learn she counts turtles to avoid counting her own heartbreaks after a broken engagement. Her sanctuary faces an incoming luxury resort bid. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness disguised as purpose.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The coastal research consortium launches an anonymous pen-pal program meant to pair strangers across departments; a clerical error pairs two rivals instead. Elodie writes a first letter meant to be polite and it comes out sharp. Beat: reluctant hope.

chapters.title: Felix in the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Introduced in the rented beach house kitchen where he drafts acquisition plans at 3 a.m., disciplined and hollowed out by a father who equates money with worth. He receives Elodie's barbed letter and answers with unexpected honesty. Beat: a crack in the armor.

chapters.title: Letters Without Names
chapters.summary: Alternating POV via letters. The correspondence turns confessional: her failed engagement, his dead mother's recipes, their shared fear of being known. Neither guesses the other's identity. Beat: intimacy without risk feels safe — for now.

chapters.title: The Man from Meridian
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Felix arrives at the sanctuary as Meridian Development's lead consultant, all charm and leverage. Their in-person clash is electric and hostile; neither recognizes the stranger's voice from the letters. Beat: instant antagonism.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix offers a relocation package dressed as generosity; Elodie counters with data he can't refute. He begins doubting the project but hides it, ashamed of wavering. Beat: duty tightening its grip.

chapters.title: Salt and Static
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm strands them both at the sanctuary office overnight. Forced proximity softens the war into something warmer — still anonymous on paper, undeniable in person. Beat: attraction they refuse to name.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A poaching incident damages nests; Felix quietly uses his contacts to help, telling himself it's strategy. Elodie notices the contradiction in him. Beat: grudging respect taking root.

chapters.title: The Father's Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Flashback chapter: how Felix's father built Meridian on a collapsed marriage and bought silence with checks. Felix fears he is a copy of the original. Beat: identity dread.

chapters.title: Almost Confessions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both nearly reveal themselves in separate scenes — Elodie almost signs her letter with a detail only she would know; Felix almost tells her about the letters. Each retreats. Beat: the cost of cowardice.

chapters.title: Permit Hearing
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Public hearing where Elode testifies passionately against the rezoning while Felix sits on the developer's side of the room. Their eyes meet across the chamber. Beat: public enemies, private ache.

chapters.title: The Handwriting
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix sees Elodie's handwritten testimony exhibit and recognizes the letter writer's hand. He says nothing, now complicit in the deception. Beat: guilt curdling into self-loathing.

chapters.title: Kitchen Light
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Elodie invites 'the enemy consultant' to dinner as a truce; they cook together in her tiny kitchen and it feels like coming home to someone. Felix leaves before anything can be said. Beat: tenderness at full flood.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Meridian's board demands final signatures; Felix's father threatens to expose Felix's past failures if he stalls. Duty versus heart becomes literal. Beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: The Letter She Never Sent
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie writes a letter confessing she thinks she loves her pen pal, then burns it, deciding second chances are for people with better timing. Beat: heart armored again.

chapters.title: Exposed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the contract signing, a leaked file reveals the pen-pal pairing error — and each realizes who the other was all along. Public humiliation, private devastation. Beat: climax of betrayal.

chapters.title: What You Built Me Into
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Confrontation in the empty sanctuary: Elodie accuses Felix of collecting her secrets like assets. He cannot defend himself because the accusation is partly true. Beat: rock bottom.

chapters.title: The Resignation
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix torches his own career — kills the deal, resigns, and accepts his father's disownment — realizing power was never the inheritance he wanted. Beat: choosing identity over legacy.

chapters.title: Nesting Season
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Weeks later, hatchlings emerge; Elodie reads Felix's final anonymous letter, postmarked before everything broke, funding the sanctuary's endowment and asking nothing. Beat: grief complicated by grace.

chapters.title: The Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Felix appears at her door with no contract, no leverage, only the truth and a borrowed recipe. Elodie makes him wait on the porch until sunrise — then lets him in. Beat: forgiveness earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Epilogue-adjacent: a new season, a new survey, two sets of footprints on the beach. Elodie admits timing was never the problem — courage was. Beat: love chosen openly.

chapters.title: Felix and the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Final chapter mirrors the opening: dawn in the same kitchen, now shared, letters framed on the wall. Felix cooks breakfast while Elodie returns from the nest count. Beat: home as the answer to every theme.
